title.en: Saving Zhao with No Clean Option

dek.zh: 救兵被自己的国君叫停在半路，一个手里没有兵的公子还能做什么？
dek.en: When your own king halts the relief army halfway, what can a prince with no troops do?

heading.en: A Turn at the East Gate

paras.zh: 魏公子无忌带着百余乘车骑出了魏都大梁，准备去秦军阵前拼命，与赵国同归于尽。车过城东的夷门，他停下来见守门的老人侯嬴，把这打算原原本本告诉了他。侯嬴只送了一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车队走出几里，《史记》写无忌「心不快」；他掉转车头，回来问侯嬴。
paras.en: Prince Wuji of Wei rode out of Daliang, the Wei capital, with a hundred-odd chariots and horsemen, intending to hurl himself at the Qin army and die alongside the state of Zhao. Passing the Yimen, the eastern gate of the city, he stopped to see Hou Ying, the aged gatekeeper there, and told him the plan outright. Hou Ying saw him off with a single line — "Push on, my lord; I am old and cannot follow you". The column had gone a few li when the Records of the Grand Historian has Wuji "troubled in his heart"; he turned the chariots around and came back to question Hou Ying.

paras.zh: 难处摆在那里：秦军围住赵都邯郸，无忌自己的国君魏安釐王已经派将军晋鄙率十万大军救赵，却传令止步，把军队留在邺观望。无忌手里没有兵，只有百余乘车骑和一群门客。去是送死；不去，邯郸旦暮可下，而他的姐姐是赵国平原君的夫人。
paras.en: The difficulty was plain to see. Qin forces had invested Handan, the Zhao capital. King Anxi of Wei, Wuji's own king, had already sent General Jin Pi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao, then ordered him to halt and camp at Ye and watch. Wuji had no army, only a hundred-odd chariots and a band of retainers. Riding out meant dying for nothing. Staying meant Handan could fall any day — and his own sister was the wife of Lord Pingyuan of Zhao.

heading.en: A Relief Army That Stopped Halfway

paras.zh: 秦昭王在破赵长平军之后，进兵围邯郸。无忌的姐姐是平原君夫人，她几次写信给魏王和无忌求救。魏王于是派将军晋鄙将十万众救赵。
paras.en: King Zhao of Qin, having destroyed Zhao's army at Changping, marched on and laid siege to Handan. Wuji's sister was the wife of Lord Pingyuan. She wrote letter after letter to the king of Wei and to Wuji begging for help, and the king of Wei sent General Jin Pi with a hundred thousand troops to rescue Zhao.

paras.zh: 秦王派使者告诉魏王，把话挑明：邯郸旦夕可下，诸侯谁敢来救，等打下赵国，就移兵先打谁。魏王怕了，派人止住晋鄙，让大军驻在邺，「名為救趙，實持兩端以觀望」——名义上救赵，实际是两边看风向。
paras.en: Qin's envoy put the matter bluntly to the king of Wei: Handan would fall within days, and whichever of the other states dared to come to Zhao's relief, Qin would turn on it first once Zhao was finished. The king was frightened. He sent men to stop Jin Pi and had the great army camp at Ye — "in name a rescue of Zhao, in fact holding both sides and waiting to see which way things broke."

paras.zh: 平原君的使者一批接一批赶到魏国，冠盖相属，责备公子说：我高攀这门婚姻，是以为公子高义、能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮降秦而魏国救兵不至，这份高义在哪里？哪怕你看不起我，独不怜公子姊邪——难道连你的姐姐也不可怜吗？
paras.en: Lord Pingyuan's envoys now arrived in Wei in an unbroken stream, official carriages crowding the road, and reproached the prince in their master's name: I attached myself to this marriage because I took the prince for a man of high principle, one who hurries to relieve another's distress. Now Handan may surrender to Qin any day and Wei's rescue has not come — where is that principle? "Even if you think little of me, have you no pity for your own sister?"

paras.zh: 无忌几次请求魏王，宾客辩士说王万端，魏王畏秦，终不听。无忌自度无法从魏王那里得到兵，「計不獨生而令趙亡」——不能自己活着而让赵国灭亡，于是约集宾客，备好百余乘车骑，打算带门客去拼死。这就是他出城那天的打算。
paras.en: Wuji petitioned the king of Wei several times, and his retainers, debaters and persuaders alike, argued the case from every angle. The king of Wei feared Qin and never relented. Wuji judged that he would never get troops out of the king, and decided he would not "live on alone and let Zhao perish." So he gathered his retainers, readied a hundred-odd chariots, and meant to lead his men into the Qin lines to die with Zhao. That was the plan he rode out with.

paras.zh: 无忌平日「仁而下士」，不论贤与不肖都谦恭礼交，不敢以富贵骄人，方圆几千里的人争相投奔，门下食客三千人。有一次他与魏王下棋，北方边境举烽火报警，说赵寇将入界。魏王放下棋要召大臣商议，无忌说是赵王打猎；不久传话回来，果然如此。他说是门客能探得赵王的私事。《史记》写，此后魏王「畏公子之賢能，不敢任公子以國政」。
paras.en: Wuji's reputation rested on his habit of humbling himself before men of talent: humane and courteous to scholars whether able or not, never letting wealth and rank make him proud. Men competed to join him from a country several thousand li around, and three thousand retainers ate at his gate. Once, while he and the king were playing a board game, beacons flared on the northern frontier: "Zhao raiders are crossing the border." The king put down the game and wanted to summon his ministers. Wuji said it was merely the king of Zhao out hunting, not a raid. Before long word came from the north that it had indeed been a hunt. A retainer of mine, Wuji said, has a way of learning the king of Zhao's private business and reports it to me. From then on, the Records says, the king "dreaded the prince's ability, and did not dare entrust him with affairs of state."

paras.zh: 魏国有位隐士侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门。无忌想厚赠他，他不肯收，说自己修身絜行几十年，终不能因为守门穷困而受财。无忌于是置酒大会宾客，空出车上左边的尊位，亲自去迎侯嬴。侯嬴穿着破旧衣冠，径直登上上座，也不谦让，为的是看无忌的反应；无忌执辔，愈恭。侯嬴又下车去见他的朋友、在市上当屠户的朱亥，故意站着和朱亥说了很久，暗中观察无忌。这时魏国的将相、宗室和宾客已坐满一堂，等无忌回去开席；跟随的骑从都在暗中骂侯嬴。无忌的脸色反而越发温和，始终不变。到家后无忌请他坐上座，向在座宾客一一介绍，宾客皆惊。侯嬴后来自己说破：他这样做是想成全公子礼贤下士的名声；市人因此把他看作小人，称无忌是能下士的长者。宴罢，侯嬴成为上客。
paras.en: Wei had a recluse named Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then got down to see his friend Zhu Hai, a butcher in the market, and deliberately stood talking with him for a long time, watching Wuji out of the corner of his eye. Meanwhile Wei's generals, ministers, royal kinsmen and guests filled the prince's hall, waiting for him to begin the feast, and Wuji's own riders cursed Hou Ying under their breath. Wuji's face only grew milder; his manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he had acted this way to make the prince's name as a man who humbles himself before scholars. As a result, the townsfolk took Hou Ying for a lout and Wuji for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars. When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became one of Wuji's most honored guests.

heading.en: The Tiger Tally, the Iron Mace, and Eighty Thousand Men

paras.zh: 无忌折回夷门，侯嬴对他说，带门客去冲秦军，就像拿肉投给饿虎，毫无用处；公子待他厚，公子走而他不送，他由此知道公子会心怀不满而折回。接着侯嬴献上一个计策。晋鄙的兵符平时收在魏王卧室内；如姬最得魏王宠爱，出入卧内，有能力偷出来。侯嬴说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，她为此出资三年，从魏王以下都想替她报父仇而未能；如姬向无忌哭诉，无忌派门客斩了仇人的头献给她。侯嬴的判断是：如姬愿为公子死，只是没有机会；公子一开口，她必答应。得虎符，夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。
paras.en: When Wuji came back to the Yimen, Hou Ying told him that charging the Qin army with his retainers would be like throwing meat to a starving tiger — it would accomplish nothing. The prince had treated him generously, he said, and when the prince left without being seen off, Hou Ying had known the prince would resent it and come back. Then Hou Ying laid out a plan. Jin Pi's command tally was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber. Lady Ru, the king's favorite, came and went in the bedchamber freely and could steal it out. Hou Ying spelled out why she would. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had put up money to see her father's death avenged, and no one, the king included, had been able to bring it off. She had wept to Wuji, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and present it to her. Hou Ying's judgment was that Lady Ru would gladly die for Wuji and had simply never had the chance to serve him; one word from the prince and she would agree. Get the tally, take over Jin Pi's army, go north to rescue Zhao and push Qin back from the west — "an achievement worthy of the Five Hegemons."

paras.zh: 无忌照计行事，向如姬开口。如姬果然盗出晋鄙的兵符，交给了他。
paras.en: Wuji followed the plan and asked Lady Ru. She did steal Jin Pi's tally and give it to him.

paras.zh: 侯嬴接着提醒他最危险的一步。「將在外，主令有所不受」——即便兵符合上，晋鄙也可能不交兵权，再向魏王请示，事情就危险了。他让无忌带上屠者朱亥同行：晋鄙听从，最好；不听，让朱亥动手。
paras.en: Hou Ying then warned him about the step that could ruin everything. "A general in the field need not obey every command from his sovereign." Even if the tally matched, Jin Pi might refuse to hand over the army and send to the king instead, and then the whole thing was in danger. Hou Ying told him to take the butcher Zhu Hai along: if Jin Pi complied, well and good; if he did not, Zhu Hai could strike.

paras.zh: 无忌听了流泪，说晋鄙是「嚄唶宿將」，此去恐怕不听，那就必然要杀他，「是以泣耳，豈畏死哉」。朱亥是侯嬴早先推荐的屠者，隐于市井；无忌几次登门，朱亥不回谢，无忌当时还觉得奇怪。
paras.en: Wuji wept at that. Jin Pi was an old campaigner of the shouting, veteran stamp, he said, and would, he feared, refuse — in which case he would have to be killed. "That is why I weep — do you think I fear death?" Zhu Hai was the butcher Hou Ying had recommended earlier, a man of worth hidden in the marketplace. Wuji had called on him several times, and Zhu Hai had never once returned the courtesy, which Wuji had found odd at the time.

paras.zh: 这次朱亥答得干脆：我是市井里操刀的屠户，公子几次来问候我，我不回谢，是以为小礼无用；如今公子有急，正是我效命的时候。侯嬴则请求算着无忌的行程，在无忌抵达晋鄙军中的那天，北向自刭相送。《史记》记，后来侯嬴果然「北鄉自剄」。
paras.en: This time Zhu Hai answered without hesitation: "I am a knife-wielding butcher in the market. You have come to see me in person again and again, and I never answered in kind because small courtesies are of no use. Now that you are in a fix, this is the moment for me to give my life." Hou Ying, for his part, asked to reckon the days of Wuji's journey: on the day Wuji reached Jin Pi's army he would cut his own throat facing north, to see him off. The Records later confirms that Hou Ying did cut his throat facing north.

paras.zh: 无忌到邺，假传魏王令来代晋鄙。晋鄙合了符，仍有疑心，举手看着他说：我如今拥十万之众屯在边境，是国家重任，一辆车来接替我，是怎么回事？打算不听。朱亥从袖中抽出四十斤铁椎，椎杀晋鄙。无忌于是接管军队，下令：父子都在军中的，父亲回家；兄弟都在军中的，兄长回家；独子没有兄弟的，回去奉养父母。选出八万人，进兵击秦军。
paras.en: At Ye, Wuji presented a forged order from the king of Wei and announced that he was replacing Jin Pi. Jin Pi matched the two halves of the tally and was still suspicious. He raised his hand and looked hard at Wuji: "I hold a hundred thousand men on the frontier, a grave charge for the state, and now a single carriage comes to relieve me. What is the meaning of this?" He was on the point of refusing. Zhu Hai drew from his sleeve an iron mace weighing forty catties and killed him. Wuji took over the army and gave orders in the camp: fathers and sons both serving, the father goes home; brothers both serving, the elder brother goes home; an only son with no brothers goes home to care for his parents. From the men left he picked eighty thousand, and advanced on the Qin army.

paras.zh: 秦军解围退走，邯郸得存。赵王和平原君亲自到边界迎接，平原君背着箭袋在前面引路；赵王再拜，说自古贤人没有赶得上公子的。
paras.en: The Qin army raised the siege and drew off; Handan was saved and Zhao preserved. The king of Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came out to the border to meet Wuji in person, Lord Pingyuan with a quiver of arrows on his back, leading the way. The king of Zhao bowed twice and said that no worthier man had appeared since antiquity.

paras.zh: 赵孝成王感激他矫令夺兵而存赵，与平原君商量，要拿五座城封给他。无忌听说，「意驕矜而有自功之色」。一位门客劝他：别人对你有德，不可忘；你对别人有德，最好忘掉。矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，还自骄自功，我私下以为不可取。无忌「立自責，似若無所容者」。后来赵王以主人之礼相迎，无忌侧身辞让，自言有罪过，「以負於魏，無功於趙」。赵王因他退让，口不忍献五城，最后把鄗给他作汤沐邑，魏国也把信陵还给他。
paras.en: King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that Wuji had seized the army on a forged order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan and proposed to enfeoff him with five cities. When Wuji heard, he "showed a self-satisfied look, as if the credit were his own." A retainer came to him: kindness done to you must never be forgotten, he said; kindness you do to another is best forgotten. Forging the king of Wei's order and seizing Jin Pi's army — "toward Zhao you have done a service; toward Wei you cannot be called a loyal minister." To go on preening yourself over it is something I cannot approve. Wuji "at once blamed himself, as if there were nowhere he could hide." Later, when the king of Zhao received him with the rites of a host, Wuji stood to the side, declined the honor, and pronounced himself at fault, saying he had failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao. Because Wuji held back, the king of Zhao could not bring himself to hand over the five cities. In the end the king gave him the town of Hao to support his household, and Wei restored to him the city of Xinling.

paras.zh: 魏王对他盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，是发怒的，无忌自己也清楚。秦军退去之后，他让将领把魏军带回魏国，自己与门客留在赵国。后来平原君讥笑他与赌徒、卖浆的人交游，他辞别姐姐要离开时说「始吾聞平原君賢，故負魏王而救趙，以稱平原君」——当初听说平原君贤明，才辜负魏王去救赵，好配得上平原君。
paras.en: The king of Wei was angry over the stolen tally and the killing of Jin Pi, and Wuji knew it. Once Qin had been driven off and Zhao saved, he sent the Wei generals home with their troops and stayed on in Zhao with his own retainers. Later, when Lord Pingyuan sneered at him for keeping company with gamblers and ale-sellers, Wuji took leave of his sister to depart and said that he had first heard Lord Pingyuan was worthy, and so had failed the king of Wei to save Zhao, to live up to Lord Pingyuan.

paras.zh: 作者推断：把这件事读成“为朋友两肋插刀”，会错过它真正的难处。无忌折回夷门，本是问侯嬴自己有何过失；侯嬴却借这次折返点破赴死无益。侯嬴那句「譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉？尚安事客？」把勇气换成了计算：百余乘车骑投进秦军能换来什么？连门客都用不上，还要门客做什么。
paras.en: The author's inference: treat this as a friend staking everything for a friend and you miss where the real difficulty lay. Wuji turned back at the Yimen to ask Hou Ying what fault he had committed; Hou Ying used that return to show him that riding to his death would accomplish nothing. His rebuke — it would be like throwing meat at a starving tiger; what would it accomplish, and what use would retainers be then? — traded courage for arithmetic: what would a hundred-odd chariots buy against the Qin army? If even his retainers could not be put to use, what were retainers for?

paras.zh: 第二步是给坏情况留人手。侯嬴提醒无忌，兵符合上，晋鄙也可能不交兵权，并让他带上朱亥；无忌听后预见到这一步要杀本国的老将，所以先流泪说破。作者推断：把代价先讲明，事到临头就不是意外，而是执行——这并不等于代价变小了。
paras.en: Second, the bad case was staffed before anyone acted. Hou Ying warned Wuji that even with the tally matched, Jin Pi might refuse to hand over the army, and told him to bring Zhu Hai; hearing this, Wuji foresaw that the step would mean killing an old general of his own state, and wept and said so out loud first. The author's inference: naming the cost in advance does not make it smaller. It turns a shock into an execution of a decision already made.

paras.zh: 第三步是事成之后怎么记账。赵要封五城，门客提醒他对魏算不得忠臣，他立刻自责；在赵王面前自言负魏、无功于赵；留赵期间还说自己负魏王而救赵。作者推断：从这些言行看，这笔债他没有抹掉，军队送回魏国，自己留在赵国。不过原文也写，他留赵十年不归；魏王遣使来请，他怕魏王发怒，还禁止门下为魏使通报，留赵未必就是认下这笔债。
paras.en: Third, how he kept the books after it worked. Zhao was about to grant five cities; a retainer reminded him that he could not count as a loyal minister to Wei, and he blamed himself on the spot. Before the king of Zhao he declared he had failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao. While he was staying in Zhao he still said he had failed his king to save Zhao. On this reading he did not write the debt off: the army went home to Wei, and he stayed in Zhao. But the record also says he stayed in Zhao ten years without returning; when the king of Wei sent men to fetch him, he feared the king's anger and even barred his household from admitting the king's envoys, so staying there need not mean he was owning up to the debt.

paras.zh: 另一种做法是继续等魏王回心转意。但平原君已经说邯郸旦暮降秦。作者推断：拖下去的代价由城里的人承担；他选的不是一个干净的选项，而是当时能改变局面的一种做法，代价是杀本国将军、失信于魏王。
paras.en: The other course was to keep waiting for the king of Wei to change his mind. But Lord Pingyuan had already said that Handan might surrender to Qin any day. On this reading, the price of holding back would be paid by the people inside the walls, and what Wuji chose was not a clean option; it was one that could change the situation, at the price of killing his own general and breaking faith with his king.

paras.zh: 司马迁怎么看待此事？太史公说自己过大梁，特意去寻夷门；他称无忌为信陵君，说无忌结交岩穴隐者、不耻下交，「名冠諸侯，不虛耳」。作者认为，这份褒扬落在无忌敬重侯嬴这类隐士的一端，而不在矫令杀将上。此后的经过是：无忌留赵十年，后来秦攻魏，他在赵国结交的隐士毛公、薛公劝他：公子在赵国受重视、名闻诸侯，「徒以有魏也」——只因背后有魏国。他立刻归国为将，率五国之兵破秦；秦用重金收买晋鄙的门客毁谤他，魏王果然派人代将，他谢病饮酒，四年后病酒而死。他死后秦攻魏，拔二十城，此后十八年，秦国俘虏了魏国后来的国君。一种解释是，这段收尾把无忌的存亡与魏国的存亡写在了一起。
paras.en: What did Sima Qian make of it? The Grand Historian writes that he passed through Daliang and made a point of finding the Yimen. Calling Wuji by his title, Lord Xinling, he says Wuji's readiness to seek out recluses in mountain caves and to befriend men beneath him had good cause, and that his name stood first among the lords — no empty fame. One reading is that this praise lands on the end where Wuji honored recluses like Hou Ying, not on the forged order and the slain general. What came afterward ran as follows. Wuji stayed in Zhao ten years. When Qin attacked Wei, Master Mao and Master Xue, two recluses he had befriended in Zhao, told him that he was valued in Zhao and known among the lords only because he had Wei behind him. He went home at once to command Wei's army and led the forces of five states to defeat Qin. Qin then spent heavy sums of gold buying off Jin Pi's former retainers to slander him; the king of Wei did send a replacement to take over the army, and Wuji excused himself on illness and took to drink, dying of it four years later. After his death Qin attacked Wei and took twenty cities, and eighteen years later captured a later king of Wei. On one interpretation, this closing episode writes Wuji's survival and Wei's survival on the same line.

paras.zh: 本文只依据《史记·魏公子列传》。侯嬴献计、朱亥的答话、门客的劝谏，都是史家记述的对话，未必是逐字实录。
paras.en: This piece draws only on the "Biography of the Prince of Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian. Hou Ying's plan, Zhu Hai's reply, and the retainer's remonstrance are all speeches recorded by the historian, not necessarily verbatim transcripts.

paras.zh: 原文里的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」这类心理描写出自史家的叙述，本文照其叙述转述。
paras.en: Phrases in the original such as "troubled in his heart," "showed a self-satisfied look" and "at once blamed himself" are the historian's narration; this piece relays them as he tells it.

paras.zh: 本文所引兵数（晋鄙所将十万众、选出的八万人）都取自本传的记述。
paras.en: The troop figures cited here — Jin Pi's hundred thousand and the eighty thousand picked men — are taken from this biography's account.

scenario.zh: 你的团队遇到明显风险，决策层因为怕一个更大的对手，把已经派出去的资源停在半路观望。你手上有第一线的证据，也有两个能干的人；推动就要绕开常规流程，还可能让自己这方吃亏。
scenario.en: Your team faces an obvious risk. Leadership, afraid of a bigger rival, has stopped already-committed resources halfway and told them to hold and watch. You have front-line evidence in hand and two capable people; pushing forward means bypassing the normal chain of command, and it may cost your own side.

question.zh: 在动手之前，你最该先问的是哪一句——这是不是拿肉投饿虎，还是对方不配合怎么办？
question.en: Before you act, which is the first question to ask: is this throwing meat at a starving tiger, or what if the person who has to comply refuses?

assumptions.zh: 决策层停手是出于对更大对手的恐惧（如秦王恫吓魏王），不是不知道风险；你有可验证的一线证据和能干的人；事情若成，功劳与对自己这方的亏欠会同时存在。
assumptions.en: Leadership stopped out of fear of a bigger rival, in the way the king of Qin's threat stopped the king of Wei — not because they failed to see the risk. You have verifiable front-line evidence and capable people. If it works, the credit and the debt to your own side will both be real.

steps.zh: 一、先把送死式的冲锋换成具体计算：手里的资源投进去能换来什么；二、动手前为“对方不配合”备好人手和止损点（侯嬴让无忌带上朱亥）；三、事成之后认下对自己这方的亏欠，不把功劳记在自己账上（门客劝后无忌自责）。
steps.en: First, replace the death-ride with concrete arithmetic: what would the resources at hand actually buy? Second, before acting, line up a person and a stop-loss for the case where the other party will not cooperate — Hou Ying had Wuji bring the butcher Zhu Hai. Third, after it works, put the debt to your own side on your own account and do not bank the credit — as Wuji did once the retainer spoke to him.

alternative.zh: 也可以继续走流程、把证据递上去等批复，或者只做分内的事、不动自己的位置。作者提出：这两种做法保全了程序，但代价由被围的一方承担。
alternative.en: You could also stay inside the process, pass the evidence up and wait for approval, or do only your own job and leave your position untouched. The author's point: both preserve procedure, but the cost falls on the party under siege.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文只依据《史记·魏公子列传》；对话出自史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」等心理描写出自史家叙述。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece draws only on the "Biography of the Prince of Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian; the speeches come from the historian's account and need not be verbatim, and phrases such as "troubled in his heart," "showed a self-satisfied look" and "at once blamed himself" are the historian's narration.

preheader.zh: 偷符之前，他先折回去问了看门的老头一句
preheader.en: Before stealing the tally, he turned back and asked the old gatekeeper one question
